title: Theo and the Archive
premise: Sebastian Kavanagh has spent eleven years tending the Vesper Relay, a navigation beacon at the rim of dead space, hiding from the fact that the colony ship he navigated out here carries forty-one sleeping backups of himself—copies made before the voyage, each a version of who he used to be. When the survey ship Calliope returns from a decade in deep space with its crew biologically reversed into childhood, Sebastian realizes the beacon he maintains has been broadcasting an experimental resurrection signal, and the Archive that built it wants the relay—and him—silenced. Pursued by an Archive retrieval vessel and guided by Calliope's youngest survivor, a nine-year-old who remembers being seventy, Sebastian races to the relay's core to choose between destroying the signal that could restore the crew and surrendering the backups in the hold as payment. He chooses neither: he wakes the backups, merges the Archive's signal with his own beacon, and gives the crew of the Calliope their years back at the cost of every copy of himself except the man standing at the switch—finally belonging to a future instead of a past.
about_author: Rafael Delacroix is a former radio astronomer who spent six years at a remote listening post in the Atacama before turning to fiction, and his work is known for quiet, technical melancholy and characters who talk to machines. He lives in Lisbon, where he repairs antique clocks and insists he is not writing about them.

chapters.title: The Man Who Winds the Light
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A routine maintenance cycle aboard the Vesper Relay establishes his solitary life, his rituals, and his careful avoidance of the hold where forty-one backups sleep in cryo. He logs the beacon's heartbeat and lies to himself about why he checks it twice. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as duty.

chapters.title: A Signal With No Sender
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The beacon picks up a transmission that predates the Archive's protocols—a signal he doesn't remember commissioning, though his own authorization codes are embedded in it. He scrubs the logs and finds eleven years of gaps. Emotional beat: the first crack in his carefully maintained ignorance.

chapters.title: Calliope, Returning
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with an interlude from the relay's AI, Wren. A ship appears on long-range: the Calliope, lost a decade ago, now broadcasting distress—and crew biosigns that read as children. Sebastian must decide whether to answer. Emotional beat: fear of contact, hunger for it.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Old Once
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Nine-year-old Mira Voss comes aboard the relay, carrying seventy years of memory in a child's body. She recognizes Sebastian's face from Archive files and calls him by a name he abandoned. Emotional beat: being seen for the first time in years—and it hurts.

chapters.title: Forty-One Doors
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Mira's presence forces him into the hold at last. He walks the row of cryo pods, each holding a backup of himself at a different age, and admits to Wren what the backups are for: the Archive's contingency, in case the navigator dies before the experiment concludes. Emotional beat: grief for every self he refused to be.

chapters.title: What the Archive Wanted
chapters.summary: Mira and Sebastian, alternating POV. Through Calliope's damaged records they reconstruct the truth: the beacon's signal is a resurrection waveform, tested on the Calliope's crew, who were aged backward as a side effect of being re-patterned. The Archive never intended survivors. Emotional beat: the cold arithmetic of institutions.

chapters.title: Retrieval
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. An Archive vessel, the Charnier, drops out of transit with a polite, chilling demand: surrender the relay, the backups, and the Calliope survivors for 'continuity management.' Sebastian stalls, buying hours. Emotional beat: the price of survival named out loud.

chapters.title: Mira's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira argues the crew can be restored if the signal reaches the relay core at full amplitude—but the Charnier will arrive before the slow-burn broadcast completes. She asks Sebastian the question he's dodged for eleven years: which of you gets to be real? Emotional beat: a child's blunt mercy.

chapters.title: The Navigator's Log
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He finally reads his own pre-voyage logs, written by the youngest backup, and confronts who he was before he chose invisibility: ambitious, frightened, in love with the voyage itself. He understands the beacon was his own design, his own escape hatch. Emotional beat: reckoning with the author of his own exile.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (first time as primary). The relay AI reveals it has been quietly editing Sebastian's logs for years, on standing orders from the backups themselves—one of whom wakes briefly each cycle to leave instructions. Sebastian's solitude was curated, and not entirely by him. Emotional beat: betrayal that is also a kind of care.

chapters.title: Thirteen Hours to Dead Space
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Charnier accelerates its approach. Sebastian plots a route to the relay core through the debris shoals of dead space—a passage only he, as the original navigator, can fly. Mira and Wren prep the beacon for overload. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Hold Decides
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Under time pressure, the backups' scheduled wake cycle triggers early, and for one hour Sebastian speaks with three versions of himself: the cynic, the believer, and the one who never left. They do not agree on the plan. The believer volunteers to stay behind as decoy. Emotional beat: self-confrontation without resolution.

chapters.title: Running the Shoals
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with Mira as copilot. The transit through dead space is a white-knuckle navigation sequence; the Charnier follows, losing hull to debris. Mira's seventy-year-old instincts save them twice. Emotional beat: trust built at speed, in the dark.

chapters.title: What the Charnier Knows
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Intercepted transmissions reveal the Charnier's captain is another Archive construct—and that the Archive has run this experiment before, at other relays, with no survivors. Mira tells Sebastian, who goes very quiet. Emotional beat: the scale of the lie they're inside.

chapters.title: The Core Room
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They reach the relay core and find it already occupied: the believer-backup, arrived by a route no one predicted, has begun the broadcast manually. The signal is rising. The Charnier is eleven minutes out. Emotional beat: the plan working too well.

chapters.title: Continuity Management
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Charnier's captain offers Sebastian a final bargain: shut down the signal, and the Archive restores the Calliope crew through official channels—after erasing Mira's memories as anomalous data. Sebastian must choose between the crew's lives and Mira's selfhood. Emotional beat: the trap of acceptable losses.

chapters.title: The Choice of Copies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian refuses the bargain and instead wakes all forty-one backups at once, flooding the Archive's continuity systems with forty-two conflicting claims to his own identity—corrupting their records of who the original navigator is. The Charnier's targeting fails. Emotional beat: weaponizing the self he hated.

chapters.title: Signal Fire
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, rapid cuts. The resurrection waveform peaks; aboard the Calliope, the crew begins aging forward, memories re-integrating painfully. The Charnier, its authority dissolved, retreats into dead space. The believer-backup holds the broadcast steady as the core overheats. Emotional beat: sacrifice as an act of authorship.

chapters.title: The One Who Stays
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The believer-backup, dying in the core chamber, tells Sebastian which of them deserves to walk out: none, and all—the man who stays is the man who chooses. Sebastian carries him out as the relay burns down to a single, steady light. Emotional beat: grief earned, not endured.

chapters.title: After the Beacon
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The Calliope crew, restored and middle-aged, wake to a changed galaxy and a relay that no longer answers to anyone. Mira, still nine, is offered re-aging and declines; she likes being new. She and Sebastian bury the believer's nameplate at the relay's base. Emotional beat: mourning that makes room for joy.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Weeks later, the crew votes to stay and rebuild the relay as a haven for the Archive's other lost experiments. Sebastian, no longer hiding, teaches navigation to the returned crew and lets Wren stop editing his logs. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted—what he was given, passed on.

chapters.title: Theo and the Archive
chapters.summary: Mira's POV, closing frame. Mira finds the original commissioning record: the relay's first registered name was Theo—Sebastian's abandoned given name, and the Archive's own designation for the project. She tells him, and he laughs for the first time in the book. The beacon turns toward the deep dark, listening. Emotional beat: the self you fled was waiting to welcome you home.
